messages:
ops-bot: [INCIDENT] High per-org QPS spike detected for org_id=org-scarab (Scarab Labs). 95th pct queue depth 18s, tail latency > 3s. Auto-throttle applied: org rate set to 200 RPS (was 1200 RPS). Paging on-call.
sam: oncall — acknowledged, jumping in.
sam: quick ask — is this causing 503s or just elevated latency?
morgan: support — Scarab filed a ticket (#123456). They report search returning 503s and some timeouts in their UI.
tia: sre — seeing token-exhaust errors and worker backpressure. Auto-throttle looks like it cut them hard after a sustained burst. We can either raise org cap temporarily or gate heavy features. Raising affects global pool.
ellie: prodeng — proposal: scoped quota patch: bump org-scarab to 600 RPS with burst window and set expires_in 10m. Also gate rerank for them as a fast mitigation (reduces per-request cost).
sam: plan suggestion: 1) disable rerank_v2 for org-scarab, 2) bump org cap to 600 RPS for 10m, 3) monitor & roll back or escalate to dedicated if needed. Who will run the hotfix?
tia: I can run the hotfix. Executing admin API changes now.
tia: ```
# admin API call to bump org quota
curl -X POST https://admin.redwood.internal/api/v1/orgs/org-scarab/quota \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"rps_limit":600,"burst":1200,"expires_in_s":600,"reason":"emergency surge - Scarab"}'
```
tia: Also toggling feature-flag: disable "rerank_v2" for org-scarab:
```
curl -X POST https://admin.redwood.internal/api/v1/flags/org-scarab \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"flags":{"rerank_v2":false}}'
```
nate: cs — FYI I told Scarab support contact we're applying mitigations, ETA ~2m for visible change on their side.
sam: tia - paste API responses when you have them.
tia: admin-api => 200 OK, quota updated, flag updated. Monitoring now. :rocket:
ops-bot: metric update => org-scarab qps observed ~520, tail latency dropped under 800ms, 5xx rate trending down.
morgan: support — Scarab reports fewer 503s in their portal, UX looks better.
ellie: prodeng — good first step. Keep the 10m timer. If we see another sustained burst, plan is escalate to reserved capacity trial or route Scarab to a lower-cost quantized variant.
ryan: infra — can we add a temporary per-customer circuit-breaker in the routing plane to limit concurrent inflight tokens for repeat offenders?
tia: yes, I'll add a soft circuit at 800 token/s as a follow-up and note it in the runbook.
sam: logging actions into the incident ticket and writing follow-up items: (a) recommend per-org safety buffer, (b) adaptive burst controller tuning, (c) runbook entry for gating heavy features. Handing off to normal on-call in 20m. :thumbsup:
